summary: Issue #104 RT observability cost PoC (task T2): 26 criterion cells across 5 groups (counter/rt_bridge/overflow_policy/rt_primitives/timestamp), 3 runs on Windows 11 x64 i9-9900K 16c, rustc 1.99.0, criterion 0.8.2, warm-up 300ms/measure 1s/sample 20, BATCH=512 ops per timed iter; plus alloc-gap deterministic test and backend candidate probe (tracing/tracing-subscriber/metrics/tracy-client)

Counter instrumentation (3-run mean ns/op): disabled-baseline 1.361, flag/off 0.262 (gate closed, no increment), flag/on 3.895, always 3.872. Unconditional prepared-counter cost ~= one Relaxed fetch_add ~3.9 ns/op; +2.5 ns vs uninstrumented baseline; flag gate adds ~0.02 ns when on

rt_bridge (3-run mean ns/op): record/not_full 5.74 (run spread 4.35-6.68), record/full drop+count 5.41, drain/empty 2.45 (38% run spread, O(1) noise), drain/half 4.07 and drain/full 4.07 per record, overflows/read 0.45 (Relaxed load)

Overflow policy on same full-ring scenario (3-run mean ns/op): silent drop 0.894, count 5.404, aggregate 1.092, retire_channel leak-on-full baseline 5.403. count ~= leak baseline ~= record/full: the bookkeeping fetch_add sits next to the ring push cost. count-vs-aggregate 5x asymmetry likely counter-cell cache-line placement (unverified); absolute worst case ~5.4 ns/op

RT primitives baseline, uninstrumented (3-run mean ns/op): channel try_push 1.79 try_pop 1.12; retire 1.29 retire_overflows 0.44; clock tick 0.87 publish_tick 1.08; slot publish 83.5 slot read 18.4. A +3.9ns counter increment roughly triples try_push-class op cost in ratio terms but stays single-digit ns absolute

Timestamp (3-run mean ns/op): Instant::now 29.2, instant->epoch nanos->i64 34.6 (+5.4 conversion math), full timestamped_record 39.4, SystemTime::now 15.0 contrast. Clock read = 74% of the stamped-record path on Windows (QPC); timestamping every record at high rate is the dominant cost

Alloc coverage gap deterministic result (alloc_counter, same thread-local window mechanism as assert_no_alloc): caller_window=0 while spawned thread allocated, spawned_window=26>0, spawned_observed=true — a caller-side window provably cannot observe backend-owned-thread allocations; window must be installed on the measured thread

Backend probe (target/rt-observability-backend-probe, scratch crate, no workspace dep): tracing 0.1.44 MIT MSRV1.65 11pkgs info!-no-subscriber 0.27ns fmt-to-sink 425ns; tracing-subscriber 0.3.23 MIT MSRV1.65 14pkgs; metrics 0.24.6 MIT MSRV1.71.1 3pkgs counter!-no-recorder 4.3ns; tracy-client 0.19.0 MIT/Apache-2.0 MSRV1.70 5pkgs span! ~26ns with/without client + bundles Tracy C++ (BSD-3) needs C++ toolchain; all MSRVs < workspace 1.89

3 complete runs x 26 cells, no crashes (~2-3 min/run, under the 10-20 min plan estimate). Run-to-run |delta| of ns_per_op: p50=0.4% p90=16.4% max=38.5% (drain/empty O(1)-call noise; record/not_full 24.2%). Probe refs cross-validate bench: fetch_add 3.86 vs counter/always 3.87, Instant::now 29.3 vs timestamp/instant_now 29.2 ns/op. Raw data committed to docs/impl/exp/data/rt-observability-poc-20261023-0{1,2,3}.jsonl

Verdict recommendations for #103 PoC-gated items: telemetry=adopt prepared counter shape (~3.9ns/op acceptable, always-on simpler than flag gating); rt_bridge=keep drop-on-full+count design (5.4ns bounded, equals retire precedent); timestamp=Instant epoch-relative nanos workable but stamp sparsely (29ns/call dominates); metrics=defer (facade no-recorder ~= fetch_add but adds global recorder semantics, no consumer yet); tracing/logging=not for RT path (emit cost depends on app subscriber, 425ns with fmt); tracy-client/profiling=defer (26ns/span even without client, C++ toolchain, feature-flag only if ever needed)

PoC measurement complete: counter instrumentation is cheap and bounded (~3.9ns/op), rt_bridge record/drain paths are single-digit ns/op and the design's drop-on-full+count policy is confirmed affordable, timestamping is the expensive ingredient (~29-39ns), and all backend candidates pass MSRV/license gates with adopt/defer verdicts recorded per item

Corrected re-measurement (revision matched-work-nonzero-v2, harness_sha256 b0be85ed, job67b4cd, 3 runs of the 2 revised groups only; original 3x26 initial-condition cells frozen, other 18 cells unchanged). counter_equal_work ns/op: disabled 1.355623, flag/off 2.097160, flag/on 5.389289, always 5.342464; paired deltas vs disabled: always +3.986841, flag/off +0.741537, flag/on +4.033666. overflow_policy_nonzero ns/op: drop 1.524844, count 5.416549, aggregate 5.428234, retire_leak 5.413306. All figures are single-thread uncontended latency estimates — not hard RT bounds; cross-thread contention and end-to-end callback budget untested. Source: docs/impl/exp/data/rt-observability-poc-20261024-summary.json + corrected-01..03.jsonl

Supersedes seq2/seq4/seq10/seq11 interpretations (review findings P1/L1 unequal-work baseline, P1/L2 zero-valued fold): +2.5ns additive-overhead claim, 5x count-vs-aggregate asymmetry, false-sharing/cache-line mechanism, 'free flag' and 'max 5.4 bounded' claims are withdrawn. Corrected verdicts: Counter pair shape remains a viable candidate (~+3.99ns/op on synthetic equal-work base — not production headroom proof); new crates and applying counters to existing APIs remain deferred until consumer/DAG/ADR triggers; drop-on-full + shared count remains the recommended minimal loss signal; nonzero aggregate is the same cost class (~5.4ns) — use only when semantics demand, not on the withdrawn 5x claim; no logging callback on the RT path (arbitrary subscriber work can allocate/block — the 425ns fmt figure alone is not the disqualifier); metrics/tracy-client remain deferred (no need, no RT validation); backend micro-costs 0.27/425/4.27/~26 ns are provisional unarchived scratch observations, not adoption-grade; declared MSRVs 1.65/1.65/1.71.1/1.70 only (transitive effective MSRV untested); dep closures 9/25/3/8 incl. self per metadata snapshot rt-observability-backend-metadata-20261024.json
